draft.title: The Opium Wars
card: British traders sold opium, grown in India, to buyers in China. Many Chinese people became addicted, and silver flowed out of China to pay for the drug.
The Qing government banned the opium trade. In 1839 an official, Lin Zexu, seized and destroyed a large stock of British opium at Canton.
Britain sent warships and won the First Opium War (1839 to 1842). It won a second war in the 1850s. Britain fought to keep the trade open and to gain more access to China.
The peace treaties were called unequal because China was forced to sign them. China gave Hong Kong to Britain, opened more ports to foreign trade and paid money to Britain.
draft.remember: Britain fought to keep selling opium, and the forced treaties took Hong Kong and opened Chinese ports.

a.q: Why did Britain go to war with China in 1839?
opts: To protect its opium trade after China tried to stop it
To end the opium trade that was harming Chinese people
To take back silver that China owed to British banks
To help the Qing government fight a rebellion at home
a.why: China had banned opium and destroyed British stocks, so Britain used force to keep the trade open. Britain did not try to end the trade. It was the seller, and it fought to keep selling.
a.clue: Think about who was selling the opium and who wanted to stop it.

b.q: After the First Opium War, the Qing government signed a treaty that gave Hong Kong to Britain and opened more ports to foreign traders. Why do historians call such treaties unequal?
opts: China was forced to sign them after losing a war
China gained little from them but chose to sign
Britain had to give up land and ports in exchange
Both sides lost territory and trading rights equally
b.why: The treaties followed a British victory, so China signed under force and gave up land and ports. Having to accept the terms is what made them unequal, not a free bargain between equals.
b.clue: Ask whether China was free to refuse the terms.

a.best: To protect its opium trade after China tried to stop it

b.best: China was forced to sign them after losing a war

problems.detail: The Second Opium War ran from 1856 to 1860 and Britain fought it alongside France. 'Britain ... won a second war in the 1850s' leaves out France and the 1860 end date. A fuller line would be 'won a second war (1856 to 1860), fought with France'.

check.summary: Both questions are sound, each with one clear right answer, and the explanations match the card. The only issue is minor: the card says Britain won a second war 'in the 1850s' without saying France fought too or that the war ended in 1860.
